text:
I appreciate the sentiment but there is some nuance here worth considering:

First off, I’m not convinced that we make a good lobby. A group can make an outsized impact when it is big enough to tip the election scales like the Ultra-Orthodox or when they dominate a profession vital to the society’s functioning like the taxi drivers. International couples are not a large demographic and we are not concentrated in any specific field.

Secondly, we need to look at the electoral map to see who is both best positioned to support our interests and most likely to be represented in ANY government. It’s not smart to lock ourselves into one particular camp.

Finally, we want this country secular, accepting of immigrants and tolerant of non-Jews and their rights. This means that our interests are most aligned with those who represent new immigrants, especially the Russian-speaking sector (the Anglo sector leans National Religious and they aren’t necessarily our friends where secularism is concerned). Representatives most receptive to our arguments would probably be someone from Lieberman’s Israel Our Home. (I would suggest Evgeny Sova as a possible focal point). They’re also far more likely to gain control of the Misrad Hapnim than The Democrats.
